answer: Signing rights are a juniper ring: each operator earns one ring per epoch it stays solvent, and a new identity may only act through a ring that already exists. Rings are minted per operator, never per account, so n aliases share one ring and one vote. Every signing costs one copper ingot, and the k-th ingot drawn by an operator costs k ingots, so n heads burn n(n+1)/2 just to keep acting. Each ingot is stamped with a quill mark bound to the ring's holder; the mark cannot be copied or lent, and a forged mark voids the whole ring, so a farm cannot disguise its shared origin.
